subject: Hemera Consulting — Reference Design & Interop Validation
messages:
From: Alex Cho <alex.cho@hemera.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@hemera.com>, Danielle Park <dpark@hemera.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hemera x Redwood — Reference design & validation kickoff

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the time this morning. As discussed, Hemera is preparing a joint reference design to support our managed conversational analytics product on Redwood Dedicated. We want Redwood to validate interoperability across three modes: hosted API, dedicated pool (pinned), and VPC private deployment.

Attached is our draft reference architecture (hemera-reference-arch-v1.pdf) and an initial interop test matrix. High-level asks:
- Confirm that the KV cache behavior and shared-session semantics in Dedicated match our expected latency envelope for 2–8 concurrent sessions per replica.
- Validate your recommended quantization profile for our LLM ensemble (Hemera-P2 / Hemera-L1 variants).
- Run a short smoke test matrix you can share results for (see interop-test-matrix.xlsx).

Can we target an initial technical validation window next week? Ideally we'd get a short readout and a short list of gap items so Hemera can prioritize engineering work.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Solutions Architect
Hemera Consulting

Attachments: hemera-reference-arch-v1.pdf (application/pdf), interop-test-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-05-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hemera x Redwood — Reference design & validation kickoff

Hi Alex — appreciate the materials. Looping in Sergio (partner integrations) and Karthik (solution engineering) to scope the validation. Quick notes from a first pass:
- We can validate across hosted, Dedicated, and Private but the test harness and telemetry collection differs for each. We'll propose a two-day smoke plan for Dedicated and hosted, and a checklist-based verification for VPC (due to network constraints).
- For KV/cache semantics: need sample traffic patterns (session length distribution, token counts, prefix reuse rate).
- Quantization: we typically start with 4-bit-aware quant profiles on Hemera-P2; Karthik will confirm conservative throughput/latency expectations.

Sergio/Karthik — can you propose availability next Tue/Wed for a 90-min technical session and indicate whether you want a short pre-call to align on the testbed?

Cheers,
Evelyn
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Sergio — Tue 2027-05-25 09:00 PT works. We're attaching a small sample payload set and a trimmed test matrix for the hosted/Dedicated smoke run.

Quick answers:
- Typical session: 1–12 prompts, median 4 prompts; median prompt size 150 tokens; max seen in pilot 1,200 tokens (rare).
- Bursty concurrency target: 6 concurrent sessions sustained, spiky to 18 for 30s bursts.
- We definitely want quantization verification for Hemera-P2 and a light test for Hemera-L1 (latency/quality check).

Attachments: pooled-rlf-kpi-sample.json (application/json)

See you Tue.

Best,

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Cho <alex.cho@hemera.com>, lauren_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-25T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hemera x Redwood — Reference design & validation kickoff (smoke run notes)

Meeting notes and live observations from today's run:
- Hosted API: baseline latency 95th pct = 210ms for median prompt (150 tokens). No regressions observed.
- Dedicated (pinned pool): under configured pool (2 replicas) we saw tail latency spikes during burst windows to ~1.2s for large prompts. Killed/restarted a replica to exercise autoscaler; autoscale behaved as expected when we increased pool to 4 replicas — tail reduced to ~320ms.
- KV cache reuse: observed ~18% cache hit rate on Hemera sample traffic; benefit to token throughput modest but stable.
- Quantization: Hemera-P2 with our 4-bit-aware profile delivered ~28% throughput gain with negligible QA-delta on our automated evals. Hemera-L1 required additional kernel tuning; we logged a follow-up ticket.

Action items:
- Redwood: produce a short validation report + single-page gap list (Sergio) by EOD Wed.
- Hemera: provide a trimmed set of 10 long-form prompts for Dedicated stress test and confirm if synthetic prefix-reuse scenarios are OK.
- Both: align on VPC checklist artifacts (network CIDR, egress rules, KMS thumbprints).

--
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

- VPC: Checklist validated; Hemera still needs to provide KMS thumbprint and a test CIDR.

Attachments: hemera-reference-arch-v1.pdf, interop-test-matrix.xlsx, pooled-rlf-kpi-sample.json

Thanks all,
